Process of Communication
3
It consists of 7 elements:
Sender- idea to be shared
Encoding- ideas and facts into words, symbols, pictures or gestures 	
Message-what is being communicated, may be verbal or non-verbal
Channel- medium through which message is transmitted to the sender
Receiver- any person who notices and attaches some to a message/ destination for the message. He may be a listener, a reader or a viewer
Decoding-receiver translates  and interprets it to attain meaning
Feedback-  receiver reacts or responds to the communication sent by the sender

Features of successful Professional Communication
Communication is a non-verbal process by which information is transmitted between individuals and / or organizations so that an understanding may develop among them.
Communication is a continuous process of meaningful interactions among persons in an organization that results in meanings being perceived and understood in a desired way.
The role of the sender and receiver keeps changing in the entire communication activity.
Communication broadly includes both verbal and non-verbal forms. It is an art or technique of persuasion through the use of oral, written and non-verbal features.
It is a process which transmits and disseminates important ideas, thoughts, feelings, plans etc.

Barriers to Effective Communication -Semantic (language)
Semantic barriers are also known as language barriers. These barriers are caused due to improper communication between the sender and the receiver. Some instances of semantic barriers are:
Mother tongue influence
Poor quality of message
Difference in language
Difference in level of proficiency
Using technical language

Barriers to Effective Communication – Perceptual Barriers
Perceptual barriers exist in people’s minds based on how they perceive the world around them. They can be caused by the many cognitive biases of the human mind that prevent us from perceiving people and situations accurately. Individuals may also have their own unique biases based on previous experience and the influence of others.
25

findings: No explicit font sizes could be extracted.
slides.extracted_text:
Barriers to Effective Communication – Gender Barriers:
Gender barriers occur due to disparities in how different genders interact and are expected to communicate by society. Communication is also hampered by gender prejudices and assumptions that favor one gender over the other. 
Each gender has a different communication pattern and usually assumes that the other gender thinks and acts similarly.
26

Barriers to Effective Communication – Interpersonal Barriers:
Interpersonal barriers are any negative patterns of behavior that hinder from communicating or discourage others from communicating with you. Poor self esteem, social anxiety, arrogance makes it difficult for people to feel comfortable opening up to others. 
Lack of participation
Lack of open-mindedness
Lack of trust and transparency
Lack of patience and organization

Ensure clarity in message and look for genuine feedback
Understand others’ emotions
Understand other cultures and language variations and use the appropriate variety in the given context.
Make sure that information overload does not affect the communication environment adversely.
Maintain openness and acknowledge that people have different perceptions and views regarding things.
Listen attentively to others.
Speak with clarity and conviction. 
Encourage innovative ideas and views so that people do not live in fears.
